quote: Die Eulersche diophantische Aufgabe. Siehe Legendre Zahlentheorie S. 140 Band 2.
english: Euler's Diophantine problem. See Legendre, Number Theory, p. 140, vol. 2.
topic: A list of research problems and plans: shortening Kummer's proof in cyclotomic fields, extending the Pascal hexagon's notable points, Euler's Diophantine problem, division of the lemniscate arc into a+ib parts, transferring Staude's string construction of the ellipsoid, and treating the fields √(a+bi) and ∛α to derive reciprocity laws.

triage.modern_statement: I could not pin this down. The note says only 'Euler's Diophantine problem' and points to Legendre, Zahlentheorie (H. Maser's German translation of the 3rd edition, Teubner, Leipzig 1886), vol. 2, p. 140. Euler posed many Diophantine problems, for example x^4+y^4=z^4+w^4, or finding numbers whose pairwise sums or differences are all squares. I could not see what is on that page, so I cannot say which equation Hilbert meant. Without the page, the only safe description is that this is some Diophantine equation or system attributed to Euler and treated in vol. 2 of Legendre's Théorie des nombres.
triage.answered_by: Unknown. I could not identify the specific problem, so I cannot say whether it was answered later or by whom. Nothing found links it to Hilbert's 23 published problems or the 24th problem.

evidence.claim: The German translation Hilbert cites exists: A.M. Legendre, Zahlentheorie, translated from the 3rd edition by H. Maser, vol. II, Teubner, Leipzig 1886.

triage.why: My searches confirmed only that the cited edition exists (Maser's translation, vol. II, 1886). They turned up no table of contents or scan of vol. 2, p. 140, and I hit the search tool's limit before finding one. Euler set many Diophantine problems, so the note alone does not say which one Hilbert meant. Naming one (for example the equal sums of two fourth powers) would be a guess. The next step is to look at p. 140 of Maser's vol. 2 or the matching section of Legendre's 1830 Théorie des nombres, vol. 2. Then the question can be stated exactly and its later history traced.
